title: Slumming parties and drink prices
summary: Rich visitors and sailors paid inflated prices for beer and 'Sweet Lucy' wine, and the workers split the take.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: It was terrible. Well I see them big rich men, Bill, used to come there, they paid $50, $100 a head to see them kind of thing. They come in a group, they call it Self Out On A Good Time, slumming they call it, and they call it some money for that one night slumming. Yeah. Well, in them days you had rough top beer that was selling for $0.05 a pint bottle. A quart was $0.50. Budweiser beer was selling for $0.50, we used to charge them a dollar. The rough top bottle beer was $0.05, we would charge them a quarter. Well see that money, we used to work that with them women out there, you know? They'd give them that price and then we'd divvy up after everything was over and they was ready to turn in. Well we'd go around and collect our little divvy, you know, and they'd take the other half, you see? Well that's where you made your money. It wasn't so much on the tips. But when you got any good with them people out there and you work up a deal, well they used to catch most of them fell what they used to call chummies off the ship. You see? Well that's where we used to work them deals with them.
Were they just ordinary sailors or what that came out of the ship?
Well, regular sailors and seamen. Sailors and seamen.
Mr. Bell, you want to answer that?

Yeah, that ain't for me, that's where they grow up in there. That's on the two rings. They used to work that on the sailors and seamen. And they used to, well, they'd never, see like at night time they never order canned beer. Because canned beer was too cheap. Yeah.
I didn't know they had canned beer in those days, did they?

Oh yeah. You get a regular, we had regular cans about that high, about that big around. You get a half a can of beer for a nickel. You fill it up for a dime. They used to sell wine the same way. Get a half a can of wine for a nickel. Well they call it Sweet Lucy because they had syrup put in and they give it the name of Sweet Lucy.

The other women get out there in Harlem and say, bring me a half a can of Sweet Lucy. Well you know what that meant? There was a wine, clavard wine or port wine and syrup. But in the daytime, now that was in the daytime, but at nighttime was nothing but bottled beer, no wine. Everything was bottled beer.
Because they was charging a higher price for it. But if a guy had had sex, he wanted to drink a beer, he'd go in the bar room and get it over the bar, he'd get it for a nickel. Yeah.
